items.title: Singular knots and Vassiliev derivatives

references.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Vassiliev Invariants

items.statement:
Fix the round metric and orientation on $S^3$. An **$m$-singular oriented knot** is a smooth immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$ with exactly $m$ distinct transverse double points and no other self-intersections; each double-point image has exactly two preimages with linearly independent tangent vectors, and the preimage pairs are disjoint. The knot has no framing. Choose disjoint small balls around its double points, each containing no other part of the singular knot. At each double point there are two **resolutions**, obtained by separating the two local branches in the ball; label them $+$ and $-$ so the resolved crossing signs are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ under the convention that, in a diagram whose positive viewing normal agrees with the ambient orientation, the sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ and the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$.

A **framed oriented knot** is a smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ together with a homotopy class through nowhere-zero smooth sections of its oriented rank-two normal bundle. For an immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$, including one with double points, define its branchwise normal bundle over the parameter circle by $\nu_K:=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$, oriented so that a positive tangent followed by a positive normal basis gives the ambient orientation. Because $dK$ has rank one at every parameter, its image is locally a smooth line subbundle and this quotient is locally a rank-two bundle. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the framed clauses below, so these normal quotient bundles have their smooth vector-bundle structures. A **framed $m$-singular knot** has finitely many transverse double points and finitely many simple zeroes of a smooth section of $\nu_K$, all disjoint; its number $m$ of singularities is the number of double points plus the number of zeroes. A simple zero is one at which the derivative of the section in an oriented local trivialization is nonzero. Resolve double points as above, extending the normal section over the local resolution balls; each resulting section determines a framing homotopy class. To resolve a framing zero at parameter $t=0$, choose the oriented normal trivialization so the section is $t e_1$ near $0$, with $e_2$ the positive quarter-turn of $e_1$; replace it by $t e_1+\delta e_2$ or $t e_1-\delta e_2$ for sufficiently small $\delta>0$. These are the $+$ and $-$ resolutions of that zero and determine the framing classes on the resolved knots.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For an $R$-valued ambient-isotopy invariant $V$ of unframed oriented knots and an $m$-singular knot $K$, its **finite difference** is
$$
D_mV(K):=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}^m}\left(\prod_{i=1}^m\epsilon_i\right)V(K_\epsilon),
$$
where $K_\epsilon$ resolves singularity $i$ positively when $\epsilon_i=+1$ and negatively when $\epsilon_i=-1$. For $m=0$, set $D_0V(K)=V(K)$. The same formula defines $D_mV$ for an invariant of framed knots on framed singular knots, counting both double points and framing zeroes among the $m$ singularities. For one double point it reads $V(K_+)-V(K_-)$; the zero resolutions use the local normal-section model just specified. An invariant has **type at most $n$** if $D_{n+1}V$ vanishes on every $(n+1)$-singular object in its category. It has **exact type $n$** if it has type at most $n$ but not type at most $n-1$. Type at most $-1$ means the zero invariant, so a nonzero type-at-most-zero invariant has exact type zero. For an unframed link, replace $S^1$ by a finite disjoint union of oriented circles, allow marked self- or mixed double points, and use the same resolution sum. For a framed link, take a normal section on each component and count its simple zeroes together with all double points.

items.title: Weight-system integration proof boundary

references.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Vassiliev Invariants
Sergei V. Chmutov and Sergei K. Lando, Mutant knots and intersection graphs, Algebraic & Geometric Topology 7 (2007), 1579–1598

items.statement: The converse integration theorem is a separate established result: over $\mathbb Q$, every unframed weight system is the top symbol of a finite-type knot invariant, by the Kontsevich integral. For every characteristic-zero field $k$, the same existence follows from the rational theorem by the finite-dimensional scalar-extension argument below. The Kontsevich integration proof itself belongs to the later authoring pair KT-35 and is not supplied here. This converse is not a premise for the KT-34 symbol theorem or its local relations, and it is an established theorem rather than an open problem.

items.title: The four-term relation from singular Reidemeister III

references.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Vassiliev Invariants

items.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $n\ge0$. In the unframed category, let $V$ be an $R$-valued invariant of type at most $n$. In the framed category assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and let $V$ be an $R$-valued framed invariant of type at most $n$. In either category, every degree-$n$ chord diagram $D$ has an $n$-singular representative $K$ with no framing zeroes in the framed case, and $w_V(D):=D_nV(K)$ is independent of the representative and of its zero-free framing class. For every degree-$n$ 4T generator $D_1-D_2+D_3-D_4$, the induced values satisfy $w_V(D_1)-w_V(D_2)+w_V(D_3)-w_V(D_4)=0$; this holds in the framed category with no 1T condition.

items.title: The one-term relation and framing

references.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Vassiliev Invariants
Mohamed Elhamdadi, Mustafa Hajij, and Kyle Istvan, Framed Knots, arXiv:1910.10257v6 (2020)

items.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge1$, and let $V$ be an $R$-valued invariant of unframed oriented knots of type at most $n$. Then $D_nV(K)=0$ whenever the degree-$n$ chord diagram of the $n$-singular knot $K$ has a chord that intersects no other chord. This is the 1T vanishing law for unframed symbols. In the framed category no universal 1T vanishing law holds: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, integer-valued framed self-linking has type at most $1$ and has derivative $2$ on a one-chord diagram with blackboard framing.

items.title: Vassiliev invariants induce weight systems

references.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Vassiliev Invariants

items.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $n\ge0$. For an unframed $R$-valued invariant $V$ of type at most $n$, the degree-$n$ derivative induces an $R$-linear functional on degree-$n$ chord diagrams modulo 4T and 1T. For a framed $R$-valued invariant $V$ of type at most $n$, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; its degree-$n$ derivative induces an $R$-linear functional on degree-$n$ chord diagrams modulo 4T. Framed derivatives are not subject to a universal 1T vanishing law: integer-valued framed self-linking has value $2$ on the one-chord diagram with blackboard framing.

title: Vassiliev invariants and chord diagrams — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Writhe is not an unframed knot invariant

references.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Vassiliev Invariants

items.statement: For every oriented knot diagram $D$, the writhe $w(D)=\sum_c\operatorname{sgn}(c)$, with $\operatorname{sgn}(c)=\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ in the oriented projection plane with positive viewing normal, is unchanged by unframed Reidemeister moves and therefore defines an unframed finite-type invariant of type at most $1$.

items.title: The degree-one derivative of linking number

references.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Vassiliev Invariants

items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For an oriented two-component link $L=L_1\cup L_2$, let $\operatorname{lk}(L_1,L_2)$ be one half the sum of the signs of all crossings between distinct components, using $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ in the oriented projection plane with positive viewing normal. Extend the singular finite-difference formula to links by resolving marked crossings independently. At one marked mixed crossing, the positive-minus-negative derivative of $\operatorname{lk}$ is $+1$; reversing the order of those two resolutions gives $-1$. A marked self-crossing has derivative $0$. At any two distinct marked crossings, mixed or self, the second derivative is $0$, so linking number is a type-at-most-one invariant of two-component links and, by the nonzero first derivative, has exact type one. The total pairwise linking number of a one-component knot is $0$, because the defining sum over distinct component pairs is empty.
